proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 08:36 on 17 June. Only one post sits in the queue against 47 published, meaning the pipeline that keeps content flowing is broken. The quiz saw one session load the intro and immediately leave — no content reaching new readers compounds that problem. Two CI failures in 24 hours (Funnel-Hack Digest also failed) suggest a shared dependency or environment issue worth ruling out first.
proposals.proposal: Check the Daily Blog Post workflow logs for the root cause — likely a missing secret, a changed API key, or a Node version drift given both workflows failed on the same day. Fix the specific failure line, confirm the Funnel-Hack Digest failure shares the same root cause, and re-run. Do not touch the workflow file structure; a single environment variable correction or runner version pin is the target change.

proposals.impact: capitalise on 66.67% open rate with a sharper call to action
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation is the standout performer: 66.67% open rate from 12 sends, beating Money Avoidance (52.63%) and Money Worship (37.5%) by a meaningful margin. Money Vigilance readers are paying close attention. That attention is worth more if the email they open leads somewhere concrete — a quiz, a blog post, a coaching conversation. High open rate with no downstream conversion data suggests the email body ends without a clear next step.
proposals.proposal: Add one grounded, specific call to action at the close of the final Money Vigilance sequence email. The ICP here is someone who monitors their money carefully but still does not move — they need an invitation that matches their actual behaviour, not a cheerful nudge. Reference the quiz or a specific blog post (the "scared I'll fail again" post published 6 June fits this reader). One sentence. No preamble.
proposals.current_text: If any of this feels familiar, that's worth sitting with.
proposals.new_text: If any of this feels familiar, the quiz takes four minutes and tells you exactly which pattern is running the show: wayofwealth.co.uk/quiz

proposals.impact: reduce zero-start drop-off by lowering the first-screen ask
proposals.observation: The quiz had one session in 48 hours. That session loaded the intro screen and left without starting. The furthest_step_distribution shows intro_load: 1 and nothing beyond. The intro screen is the entire conversion problem right now — the person arrived, read whatever is on that screen, and decided not to begin. That is a copy or friction problem on a single component, not a traffic problem.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the intro screen's opening line and the start-button label. The current text almost certainly makes an implicit promise that feels large ("find out your money personality" style). Replace it with something that names the actual, small, observable act: four questions about real decisions, not an identity diagnosis. The button label should be a verb phrase tied to what the person does next, not what they will discover.
proposals.current_text: Discover your Money Script — the hidden pattern shaping every financial decision you make.
proposals.new_text: Four questions about how you actually handle money. No scoring system, no type labels — just a clearer picture of what's going on underneath.
